title: HAProxy ACL Bypass with URL Fragment and python-jwt Token Forgery for Privilege Escalation
vuln_pattern: Access control bypass via URL fragment (#) in HAProxy (CVE-2023-45539) allows reaching a blocked endpoint to obtain a JWT. The JWT is processed by python-jwt 3.3.3 which contains a signature bypass vulnerability (CVE-2022-39227) enabling role escalation by embedding a tampered payload inside a crafted JSON string.
fingerprint: HAProxy ACL configuration line `http-request deny if { path_beg,url_dec -i /api/v1/get_ticket }` (exposed via error or config)
Endpoint `/api/v1/get_ticket` returns JWT when accessed with fragment
Authorization header contains a JSON object instead of a standard Bearer token
exploit_steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/get_ticket# (with trailing #) to bypass the HAProxy ACL and obtain a valid guest JWT token.
Extract the token from the JSON response (key `ticket:`).
Split the JWT into header, payload, and signature parts (base64-encoded).
Decode the payload, change the `role` claim to `administrator`.

Re-encode the modified payload to base64 (without padding, using URL-safe encoding) and construct a fake JSON token string that exploits python-jwt's parsing: `{' ' + header + '.' + fake_payload + '.":"","protected":"' + header + '", "payload":"' + payload + '","signature":"' + signature + '"}'`.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/flag with the forged token in the Authorization header (raw JSON, not Bearer).
Read the flag from the response.
